node.title: Re^4: Go to perl::critic
node.author: Anonymous Monk
node.doctext: But a labeled block is a single loop, that <tt>redo</tt> makes infinite. I said outside loops is where <tt>goto</tt> comes in really handy. I only seem to ever want <tt>goto</tt> when extending the handling of STDIN of an existing script. Maybe my mind was poisoned by early exposure to BASIC or I just like that Perl has a feature of FORTRAN. Sometimes out of sheer boredom I'll write sweet spaghetti code on purpose because it's fun and easy and, as we all know, good Perl scripts tend to be so perfect they don't require maintenance. =)
